hints.content:
We can map a figure onto a **similar** figure using only rigid transformations and dilations. This means the figures must have exactly the same shapes, but may have different sizes.

For triangles in particular, two triangles are similar if all of their corresponding angles are [[☃ definition 1]].

options.definition: Angles with the same measure that we can map onto each other using rigid transformations

hints.content:
Triangle $ABC$ has angle measures of $115^\circ$ and $35^\circ$. The third angle measure is therefore $180^\circ - 115^\circ - 35^\circ = 30^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Angle A is one hundred fifteen degrees. Angle B is thirty-five degrees. Angle C is thirty degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $TUV$ has angle measures of $30^\circ$ and $113^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 30^\circ - 113^\circ = 37^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle TUV$ is not similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle T U V. Angle T is one hundred thirteen degrees. Angle U is thirty-seven degrees. Angle V is thirty degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $WXY$ has angle measures of $35^\circ$ and $115^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 35^\circ - 115^\circ = 30^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle WXY$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle W X Y. Angle W is one hundred fifteen degrees. Angle X is thirty-five degrees. Angle Y is thirty degrees.

hints.content: In conclusion, only $\triangle WXY$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.
